ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against Canadian sanctions lists administered under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; also screening against the OFAC SDN list for secondary sanctions risk, FINTRAC's consolidated list, and domestic BC high-risk political exposure categories; enhanced due diligence mandatory for foreign PEPs; ongoing continuous screening required on daily basis post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online and Registry Online Services (via gov.bc.ca/corporateonline)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be recognizable and pronounceable in English or French; if a foreign script is used, a certified transliteration and translation must be provided; the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', or 'ULC' must appear in English/French; names only in foreign characters are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name reservation is rejected, file a new name request via BC Corporate Online after reviewing the Notice of Revocation; for appeals of an unfavorable decision, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director under the BC Business Corporations Act (s.2), completing the applicable 'Reconsideration of Name Refusal' form and paying the fee (CAD 100); decision typically issued within 10 business days; if still refused, judicial review in BC Supreme Court is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office permitted only if the registered office is a physical street address within British Columbia, not a post office box; the registered office can be the address of a licensed corporate services provider, but all statutory mail and legal process must be physically collectible at that address; home offices are allowed if disclosed and physically accessible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~3-5% annual probability) for standard low-risk software publishing activity (ISIC 5820); however, unannounced inspections increase substantially if FINTRAC, CRA, or BC Registry flags money laundering indicators, inconsistent records, or high-risk PEP involvement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, ss 10, 11, 22, 51, 174 (British Columbia)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services Division, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Incorporation Application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for a BC Unlimited Liability Corporation; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine, and no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT the subscribers set out in the Incorporation Application be allocated and issued one Common Share each upon receipt of the agreed subscription amount. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the registered and records office of the Company be established at [address] in British Columbia, effective immediately. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the individuals named in the Notice of Articles shall be appointed as directors, and the following persons are appointed as officers: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary. The directors and officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute account instructions, and complete ancillary filings necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Reservation Request for the proposed ULC name, review any name conflict notices, and secure the statutory 56-day name reservation period.
required_dossiers: Consent from any person whose name or trade mark appears in the proposed corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, submit alternative name choices on a revised reservation request and request reconsideration through CORES.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles, Notice of Articles and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel / BC Registries filing checklists
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles and Notice of Articles in accordance with the Business Corporations Act, identify the first directors, prepare consent-to-act forms, and confirm the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of the Unlimited Liability Corporation
Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries any document, amend the affected schedule and resubmit the corrected form within the response period stated in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with BC Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online portal (or paper filing to BC Registries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Incorporation Application together with the Notice of Articles, signed Articles and the prescribed filing fee using online payment or recognized e-payment methods.
required_dossiers: Filing fee of CAD 350 (or equivalent USD payment as accepted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice is issued, cure the deficiency within 21 days by filing corrected documents or provide a written explanation to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Certified Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registry will review the application, record the ULC and issue the Certificate of Incorporation; request a certified extract of the Notice of Articles for banking and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the service standard, escalate to the senior registrar through the BC Registries customer service channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Corporate Records and Governance Binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the statutory minute book, register the initial share allotment, maintain the share register, adopt the corporate seal if desired, and retain the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate records contain omissions, remedy by preparing a correcting resolution and filing a change form with the registry where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Tax Authorities and Municipal Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and BC Provincial Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number, register for GST/HST and payroll program accounts if applicable, and obtain any municipal business licence required for operating from a British Columbia address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application, correct the relevant fields and resubmit; late registrations are accepted retroactively with possible penalty relief on a voluntary disclosure basis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable — digital software publishing; municipal business licensing division handles commercial occupancy permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing permit required for ISIC 5820 online game publishing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment required for virtual digital goods publishing
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to software product itself; office e-waste and electronic equipment disposal must comply with BC Recycling Regulation and municipal waste bylaws

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Commercial occupancy permit and fire safety inspection under the BC Fire Code; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance for any physical office or data-centre support premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes including GST/HST and British Columbia Ministry of Finance for provincial matters; primary portals at canada.ca/cra and gov.bc.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities including ULCs obtain a Business Number (BN) through the CRA online business registration portal at canada.ca/cra. Foreign entities must register for a Canadian tax identification number prior to any taxable activity in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Canadian tax law; entity classification follows the legal form of the Unlimited Liability Corporation under British Columbia corporate statutes. Hybrid mismatch rules apply in cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/PST (Goods and Services Tax / Provincial Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual taxable supplies for GST registration; BC PST registration threshold is CAD 30,000 for goods and CAD 30,000 for services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API requirements, or digital stamping mandated; GST/HST registrants must issue compliant tax invoices and maintain records for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services supplied to non-residents or performed outside Canada qualify for 0% GST/HST rate provided the supply is not consumed domestically. For MMORPG in-app purchases, zero-rating applies if the service is exported to non-residents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to CRA audit; penalties equal to 200% of tax evaded, plus interest and potential criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. There are no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no Central Bank approval is required for inbound capital injection, profit remittance, dividend distribution, or intercompany settlement. The principal regulatory overlay comprises the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), administered by FINTRAC, and the Investment Canada Act for foreign investment screening of direct acquisitions of a Canadian business. Profit remittance by way of dividends from a BC ULC to a non-resident shareholder faces Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, but no foreign exchange authorization. Sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act may restrict convertibility of transactions with designated jurisdictions, requiring enhanced screening for any payment counterparty. The elimination of mandatory conversion ratios applies equally to export receipts and to all cross-border gaming and app store proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canadian law does not impose any statutory timeline for surrender of export proceeds and does not mandate conversion of foreign currency into Canadian dollars. Exporters and digital publishers may retain receipts in USD, EUR, or other currencies in resident or non-resident bank accounts. However, under FINTRAC rules, any cross-border wire transfer equal to or greater than CAD $10,000 must be reported, and records must be kept for five years. The Bank of Canada does not perform guarantee or conversion of proceeds for private exporters. The absence of an export surrender regime is a positive structural factor for the treasury architecture of a global MMORPG publisher.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational sub-accounts, but not as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) can be used for low-value disbursements and app store payout aggregation, provided they are registered as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) in their respective jurisdictions and, if soliciting Canadian clients, registered with FINTRAC. The legal constraints include: FINTRAC MSB registration for any Canadian-facing activity, provincial licensing requirements in certain provinces (e.g., BC under the Money Services Act), inability to access Canadian deposit insurance (CDIC), restrictions on holding client funds in pooled clearing accounts, and the risk that offshore EMIs fall outside the OSFI-regulated banking perimeter. Therefore, core operating liquidity and any inbound equity injection should be held with a Schedule I Canadian bank, while EMIs may serve contingent-rail overflow or wallet-payout settlement for international freelancers and content creators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted, subject to enhanced due diligence, but Canadian Schedule I banks commonly require at least one director or senior officer with authorization to sign to complete a live video identity verification for non-face-to-face KYC. For British Columbia ULCs where the majority of directors are non-resident, the banks may request in-person verification at a Canadian bank branch or with a Canadian notary public/consular officer, and may require all directors to provide a physical Canadian business address for service of process. In practice, an entirely remote onboarding can be achieved by utilizing walk-in CLIENT ID verification at the bank's foreign correspondent? No, the bank's KYC policy may still require authorized signatories to be present at the Canadian branch when the account is opened. Therefore, a physical presence mandate is not statutory but is institutionally imposed for high-risk/offshore-owned pass-through entities. A hybrid solution is recommended: one resident Canadian director (or local attorney-in-fact) visits the branch to complete the interview, while non-resident directors use electronic identity verification and notarized corporate resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from ULC pass-through attributes and non-resident ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry certificate from BC Corporate Registry; full ultimate beneficial ownership diagram through the parent entity; notarized resolutions confirming the business purpose of the ULC; shareholder agreement and any check-the-box election under US tax law proving the ULC's tax-transparent or taxable classification; sworn source-of-funds declaration from the ultimate parent; audited financial statements of the parent for the last two years; details of the ISIC 5820 MMORPG publishing operations and active business conduct.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-jurisdiction inbound app store settlement flows from Apple App Store and Google Play
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform agreements with Apple and Google; payout statements demonstrating the commercial reality of MMORPG in-app purchase revenues; penetration and user-revenue geography report; clear reconciliation methodology between app store net proceeds and bank account credits; AML risk-rating questionnaire demonstrating low-risk classification for software publishing; sanctions screening policy and results for all settlement counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from foreign parent exceeding CAD $50,000 (FINTRAC reportable wire) and potentially triggering Investment Canada Act notification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions authorizing the share issue and capital call; intercompany subscription agreement; foreign exchange contract confirming conversion of initial funding currency to CAD; statutory declaration of the purpose of the capital injection (general working capital and app store settlement reserves); Investment Canada Act notification receipt or exemption confirmation from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada; transaction reference number from SWIFT; proof of no involvement of sanctioned persons or jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability of shareholders creating third-party liability ambiguity and inadequate ring-fencing of treasury assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming the unlimited liability scope and creditor exposure; bank-account side letter restricting account access to authorized treasury team; corporate indemnity and director/officer liability insurance policies; segregation of treasury accounts from operational escrow accounts; rigorous lender/creditor distancing documentation showing that the bank account is not a guarantee vessel; clean corporate search and no pending litigation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore digital EMI accounts for cross-border disbursements and intercompany settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organization chart of all EMI accounts and their legal ownership; FINTRAC MSB registration evidence for each EMI; copies of EMI client agreements and fee schedules; source-of-funds justification for each cross-border wire to the EMI; reconciliation trial balance between bank wires, EMI balances, and underlying trade settlements; sanctions screening of all EMI counterparties; clear treasury policy limiting EMI balances to operational float below CAD $100,000 to avoid concentration risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant protocol for inbound capital injection into a BC ULC is an international SWIFT MT103 wire in CAD or USD to the ULC's designated Operating Account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The payment originator must include a clear narrative purpose code: 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION', 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION', or 'INJECTION OF SHARE CAPITAL'. If the parent deposits more than CAD $100,000, the receiving bank will require a copy of the board resolution, share certificate, and a completed Income Tax Act Part XIII exemption certificate (NR301 form) to support treaty-based or exempt treatment of future remittances. The bank verifies the beneficiary ULC's legal name is an exact match to the BC corporate registry, the account number, and the country of origin. Funds originating from a foreign parent may be held in a Capital Escrow Account if the parent wishes to legally condition release of capital on satisfaction of operational milestones, but this is not mandatory. For an internationally distributed MMORPG business, the bank may require a statement affirming that the inbound transfer is not linked to sanctions targets. All wire records must be archived for FINTRAC AML compliance and for future audit trail mapping.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the ULC will use three clearing rails depending on counterparty. First, SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payments, intercompany royalties, contractor salaries, and subscription licensing fees exceeding USD $10,000. Second, wire transfers via the bank's online international remittance portal for smaller payments, executed in original currency or auto-converted CAD. Third, commercial letters of credit (UC/LC) are not typically used for ISIC 5820 software publishing trade settlements because no physical goods are shipped, but a standby letter of credit (SBLC) may be required by certain corporate partners (e.g., for cross-promotional licensing or brand collaboration) to guarantee prepaid rights; this can be issued by the Schedule I bank. For app store proceeds repatriation, Apple App Store and Google Play payout to the ULC's bank account in the beneficial territory is treated as a 'merchant settlement', not a formal documentary like a commercial LC. All outgoing remittances are subject to FINTRAC reporting if equal to or above CAD $10,000 within a single 24-hour period or sequential payment scheme. Payment packaging should avoid splitting payments to evade reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies where convertibility constraints are encountered (e.g., emerging-market settlement currencies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (15% federal Part I general rate + 12% BC provincial corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays available; preferential incentives include the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (15% to 35% of eligible expenditures at federal level) and the BC Interactive Media Tax Credit (17.5% of qualified BC labour for eligible interactive digital media products); small business deduction (13% federal + 2.4% BC on first CA$500,000 of active business income) may apply only if the ULC is a Canadian-controlled private corporation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically through CRA Corporate Internet Filing (E-file) or approved commercial EFILE software; BC provincial tax is integrated with the T2 via the BC provincial corporate tax schedule
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due no later than six months after the fiscal period end; final tax balance payable no later than two months after year-end for non-CCPC taxpayers and three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the small business deduction; quarterly instalments may be required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for income tax purposes (before losses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must compute Canadian-source income under Part I, exclude foreign-source revenue, and attach any applicable s.216 election to limit tax liability for ULC pass-through treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions from net income, including capital cost allowance, reserves, and non-operating outlays.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only claim deductions permitted by statute; maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for transactions with non-resident shareholders to avoid denial under s.247.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying loss carry-backs and carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the ULC's Canadian-source taxable income is accurately isolated; do not include passive foreign income if the s.216 election is in force.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax payable before provincial allocation and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an eligible ULC, Part I tax may be computed as if each shareholder were the corporation entity; provide the required election and shareholder information schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC provincial corporate tax allocation, provincial credits, and resulting BC tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion taxable income to BC using the applicable allocation formula; claim BC Interactive Media Tax Credit only for payroll and activity performed in BC; report all BC-source income from local MMORPG development and app-store receipts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s.162(1) of the Income Tax Act is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat failure increases the penalty by 10% under s.162(2); false statements or omissions trigger a s.163(2) penalty of 50% of the understated tax; daily compound interest applies on outstanding balances and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced withholding rate under an applicable income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must provide the payer with a completed NR301 or equivalent treaty-benefit statement plus a valid tax-residency certificate (TRC) issued by its residential tax authority before payment; treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses, beneficial ownership, and Canadian GAAR (s.245) must also be respected; withholding documentation must be retained for audit by the CRA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for both interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to exceptions and treaty reductions. Under the Canada–US treaty, arm's-length interest is generally 0%, and royalties are limited to 10%, with certain copyright/software royalties potentially 0%; other treaties vary from 10% to 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canadian TP rules require filing Form T106 when non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate per year; contemporaneous master file and local file are expected for all large transactions above this threshold, and mandatory country-by-country reporting applies when consolidated group revenue is at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulation comparable to offshore zero-tax jurisdictions; however, general anti-avoidance rules (s.245 GAAR), Canadian residence tests, treaty anti-abuse clauses, and CRA anti-shell/economic substance enquiries require the ULC to demonstrate real physical presence, payroll, and decision-making in BC; treaty-shopping or shell arrangements without substance are vulnerable to re-characterization, denial of treaty relief, and Part XIII deficiency assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of worldwide or Canadian-source revenue, false deductions, fabricated books, or deliberate destruction of records in relation to in-app purchase income and global MMORPG sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax evasion under s.238 of the Income Tax Act carries a fine of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; s.239 false-statement penalties reach 50% of the understated tax; Criminal Code fraud charges add independent penalties including imprisonment up to 14 years where fraud exceeds CAD 5,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are subject to civil restitution for withheld amounts and unpaid corporate taxes; the corporate veil may be pierced where the ULC is a mere sham or vehicle for evasion; personal asset freezes, travel bans, denial of federal/provincial licenses, and imprisonment of directors can follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a BC unlimited liability corporation (ULC) with no real office, staff, or board activity in BC, and relying on treaty reductions to repatriate passive profits extracted from global MMORPG operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under s.245 eliminates the tax benefit and re-determines liability; treaty relief may be refused; recharacterized payments attract 25% Part XIII withholding plus interest; false declarations trigger s.163(2) penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders of a BC ULC may face unlimited liability for corporate obligations and unpaid taxes where veil-piercing applies; directors who authorized artificial non-resident structures are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes and may be subject to ministerial certificates of personal tax liability, travel prohibitions, and civil seizure orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as a money services business or to implement FINTRAC compliance when processing large-volume global app-store payouts, digital wallet settlements, or in-game crypto-currency secondary markets; failing to report suspicious transactions or large virtual currency transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for corporations and CAD 100,000 for individuals under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; criminal enforcement may include imprisonment up to 5 years, cease-and-desist orders, and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers of the ULC are personally liable unless they establish due diligence; knowing involvement in unlicensed money services business can lead to criminal convictions, personal fines, director disqualification, and international travel notification or bar orders.
